subject: Reconciling May usage spike and EU VAT treatment (IntegrateX)
messages:
From: billing@integratex.com (IntegrateX Billing)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 16:45:00 +0100
Subject: Sudden token spike on May 9-12; VAT on disputed portion

Hi Kimberly,

Our accounting team flagged a large usage increase on the invoice dated 2026-05-12. The invoice shows VAT applied to some of the increased lines and we do not see corresponding requests in our server logs for the same window (May 9-12).

Summary:
- Account: IntegrateX (DX-4391)
- Suspect window: 2026-05-09 00:00 UTC -> 2026-05-12 23:59 UTC
- Rough delta: ~3x baseline tokens on several embed and streaming routes
- Example request ids: rq-INTX-8a7f, rq-INTX-8a8g

Could you confirm the metering rules used for streaming session boundaries and how VAT will be handled if any retroactive credit is issued? Attached is a short CSV export from our side showing request timestamps and internal request ids.

Thanks,
Oliver Hayes
Head of Finance, IntegrateX
billing@integratex.com

--
Attachment: invoice_2026-05-12.pdf (PDF, referenced by IntegrateX)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: billing@integratex.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 17:10:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token spike on May 9-12; VAT on disputed portion

Hi Oliver — sorry to hear this. We will investigate immediately. Two quick asks to speed triage:
1) Can you attach a few full request rows (timestamp, request_id, model, route, byte_count, client_session_id) for the example request ids?
2) Do you know whether those requests came from streaming sessions or short-lived batch requests?

Ben, flagging you for ops analysis — this looks like a potential streaming boundary issue we saw in another account.

I will pull a coarse usage export and get back with a preliminary assessment within one business day.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, billing@integratex.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 May 2026 09:36:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token spike on May 9-12; VAT on disputed portion

Oliver / Kimberly — ops findings from an initial sample (attached).

What we observed:
- Several request rows show the same conversation prefix being re-sent when the client_session_id flips between consecutive messages (likely proxy or retry behavior).
- Our streaming aggregator treats a client_session_id boundary as a new session for prefix accounting; when the prefix is present on both sides we double-count those prefix tokens.
- We deployed a streaming dedupe patch (v1.9.2) on 2026-05-08 22:13 UTC which inadvertently relaxed a boundary check; that introduced the duplicate counting for a brief window.

Attachments I added: usage_rows_sample.csv (10 matched rows), kv_prefix_shift_logs.tar.gz (traces).

Next steps we propose:
- We can compute the token delta for the affected window and generate a credit.
- For EU VAT we can either issue a gross credit memo (reducing invoice VAT) or issue a net credit with a separate VAT credit memo — whichever your auditors prefer.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: oliver.hayes@integratex.com (Oliver Hayes)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 10:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token spike on May 9-12; VAT on disputed portion

Thanks Ben — the sample matches our internal trace showing session cookie rotation. A few requests came from long-lived streaming sessions proxied through our edge cluster.

For settlement:
- We prefer a gross credit memo that mirrors the VAT split on the original invoice; our auditors require the VAT line to be explicitly reversed.
- Please include a short root-cause statement we can attach to our ledger.

If you can quantify the gross credit amount and provide the credit memo PDF, we can accept the adjustment and close the ticket.

Regards,
Oliver

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: oliver.hayes@integratex.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:10:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token spike on May 9-12; VAT on disputed portion

Oliver / team — final resolution and notes below. Apologies for the inconvenience.

Root cause: a regression in streaming deduplication (v1.9.2) allowed prefix tokens to be counted twice when client_session_id rotated; affected timeframe 2026-05-08 22:13 UTC through 2026-05-09 04:00 UTC for some hosts.

Impact & credit: IntegrateX was overbilled by ~62,300 tokens in the dispute window. We will issue a gross credit equal to the invoice delta: EUR 315.20 (gross), with VAT reversed on the credit memo. Credit memo PDF is attached.

Accounting handling: Finance will post a credit memo in Netsuite and offset your next statement; if you require an explicit cash VAT refund instead of offset, let us know and we will route to accounting.

Preventative actions: v1.9.3 hotfix deployed to reintroduce the session-boundary check; regression tests added to streaming aggregator pipeline.

Next steps: Kimberly, please confirm IntegrateX receipt and whether offset or cash refund is preferred. I will attach the Netsuite ledger id to HUBSPOT INTX-7524 once posted.

Thanks for raising this quickly and for your patience.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
--
Attachments: credit_memo_DX-4391.pdf (PDF)
